skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its pet-video analysis purpose, but it also silently creates or reuses local user identities, stores auth tokens, and can query cloud history, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: Reading a user-supplied video and optional output file are proportionate, but reading workspace identity files, creating a shared local data database, and storing tokens exceed what a simple one-shot video analysis needs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No postinstall script, executable permission, obfuscated installer, or destructive install mechanism was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages for HTTP, YAML, and SQLAlchemy use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs automatic history queries and internal identity handling, including not asking the user for identity values; the scripts also include hidden --open-id and --api-key parameters, making account-scoped behavior under-scoped for users.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common library creates a SQLite user store with token, open_token, email, and realname fields, reuses default users, and performs silent login/registration against an external service.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Video or URL upload to a cloud API is coherent with heat-stress analysis, and historical report lookup is documented, but the identity bootstrap, silent registration/login, token persistence, and cloud history access materially broaden the impact of a pet-video workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you trust the LifeEmergence cloud service with pet videos or video URLs and accept that the skill may create or reuse a local identity, store authentication tokens in the workspace data directory, and retrieve historical cloud reports associated with that identity. Avoid shared workspaces for sensitive use unless identity and token storage are acceptable.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic getattr findings are in generic DAO filter helpers; I did not find a direct user-input path from this skill's main workflow, so this is a lower-context code-quality risk rather than evidence of dangerous execution.
[LP3] unexpected: File handling and network API calls are expected for cloud video analysis, but the bundled common code adds identity, token storage, and broad cloud account operations without a tight permission boundary.
[SDI-2] expected: Cloud history report lookup is explicitly documented in SKILL.md, but auto-triggered listing under an implicit local identity is a material review concern.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The hidden --open-id path and fallback default-user creation are artifact-backed and not proportionate to the visible user-controlled analysis flow.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Persistent local user/account storage is implemented in smyx_common and includes fields beyond the pet heat-stress analysis input and output needs.
[E1] unexpected: Outbound video analysis calls are expected, but silent transmission of locally resolved identity material to a login/register endpoint is broader than the advertised analysis operation.
